significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that, holding language, resource level, and entity popularity fixed, factual-retrieval accuracy decreases as "subject token count" increases, together with the form-(ii) mechanism that the loss is "causally localized to early-layer subject-token aggregation." This would predict retrieval disparities for previously untested entities and constrain whether gaps such as those measured by X-FACTR (Jiang et al., 2020) should be attributed solely to training resources; it also connects that behavioral law to the last-subject-token factual pathway implicated by ROME (Meng et al., 2022), rather than merely establishing decodability. The claim determinately establishes both a cross-lingual phenomenon and a causal mechanism; a negative within-language result would instead rule out fragmentation as an independent cause and redirect explanations toward exposure or decoding, so both branches are informative. Topic-substitution check: the general topic of language-independent versus language-specific knowledge representations would not itself earn this score—the specific controlled ordering and early-aggregation mechanism are materially more constraining than the topic-median hypothesis.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the measurable "subject token count (fertility)" as a predictor of factual-access risk and the proposed training-free interventions "subject pooling" and "retokenization/insert-space preprocessing." Fertility is ex ante because names can be screened before queries or deployment, leaving time to alter tokenization, while the mitigation is an actionable decode/preprocessing knob rather than only a post-hoc explanation. The asserted monotonic relation—"the more tokens an entity name is split into, the harder it is for the model to retrieve facts"—predicts an ordering after model-specific recalibration across multilingual models and languages, with downstream uptake by tokenizer designers and practitioners auditing or shipping multilingual systems. Topic-substitution check: deleting this predictor and intervention leaves only the broad multilingual-representation topic, which supplies neither lead time nor a design rule and would not justify the same score.
